title: Aniimo Pathfinder Talents Guide | Report Cards, Every Skill and Passive by Rank | Aniimo Guide
description: Every Aniimo Pathfinder talent explained: how Report Cards work, the active skills like Heal, Aeroboard, Mega Mallet and Bubble Gun, the passives like Master Trainer and Boss Breaker, the talents that unlock special evolutions, and which ones to pick first. Checked on Wikily, GameWith and other Aniimo guides in November 2026.
joke: In Aniimo, the Bubble Gun keeps a wild Aniimo from fainting, which is more mercy than my own team ever gets.

sections.heading: Intro
sections.script: Your Aniimo are not the only ones who grow stronger. You, the Pathfinder, have a talent list of your own, with active skills like a hover board and a giant hammer, and passives that boost experience, damage and catching. Most players unlock a few talents and never look again, even though some of them change how fast you level and how safely you catch. In this video we go through the whole Pathfinder talent system rank by rank: how Report Cards work, what each skill and passive does, which talents unlock special evolutions, and which ones are worth picking first. We compared the talent lists on Wikily and GameWith, and where guides disagree on small details we keep it rough. Stay until the end for the order we would pick them in.

sections.heading: How talents and Report Cards work
sections.script: Talents unlock through your Pathfinder rank. The rank gates sit at player levels twenty five, thirty five, forty, forty five, fifty, fifty five and sixty, and they continue up to Trailblazer. To pass a gate you finish its Elite Training course and the Promotion Assessment, and the new title opens new talents. Each rank opens a new batch of talents, both active skills and passives, and you spend Report Cards, an item you find in the Talents menu, to learn them. Guides agree that you earn Report Cards from upgrade levels, Aniilog levels, Journey quests and the Elite Pathfinder Challenge. The cost grows with the rank: the early passives cost one card, the middle ones two, and the late ones three. That means a careless early choice can leave you short of cards later, so it pays to read before you click.

sections.heading: Student one talents
sections.script: The first rank, Student one, opens at level twenty five. The active skills are Heal, which restores health to the Aniimo you have out, and the Aeroboard, a hover board that speeds up travel without using stamina. The passives here cost one Report Card each. Enhanced Twining boosts your Aniimo damage after you twine, starting around seven percent and rising to about twenty five at the top level. Elemental Boost strengthens elemental counters. Master Trainer raises Aniimo experience from catches, defeats and experience items. Mode Switch lets you change between Catch, Attack and Defense mode, and Pro Catcher unlocks the Aniipod Pro in the shop.

sections.heading: Student two and three
sections.script: Student two arrives at level thirty five. Gravity Pull moves ancient energy objects from a distance, which is how you solve the ruin puzzles. Mega Mallet is a hammer that deals heavy Break damage in a circle in front of you and smashes solid objects. The passive Boss Breaker costs two cards and adds five percent damage against Alpha and Omega bosses. Student three comes at level forty. Tweetin Target throws a rubber duck to lure wild Aniimo, and Plushie Pummel is a spinning doll attack. Quick Twine makes twining nearly instant, Elemental Ward adds resistance, and Master Catcher lets you buy stronger Aniipod types in shops.

sections.heading: The Wayfarer ranks
sections.script: Wayfarer one begins at level forty five and gives you Revive, which brings a fainted Aniimo in your party back, plus the passive Research Expert, which increases the credits you earn from reporting. Wayfarer two at level fifty brings the Bubble Gun. It keeps the target from fainting, its health stays at one while the effect lasts, so you can catch it multiple times. Nimble Dodge reduces your dodge stamina cost by ten percent. Wayfarer three at level fifty five adds Go Rubber Duck, a giant duck that lures Aniimo from a large area, and the passives Measured Strike and Sure Shot. Measured Strike adds ten percent damage to enemies in the Break state, and Sure Shot greatly extends your Aniipod range.

sections.heading: The Trailblazer ranks
sections.script: The top ranks are Trailblazer. At level sixty, Trailblazer one gives Fast Charge, which speeds up your Aniimo ultimate charging by ten percent. Trailblazer two at level sixty five adds the Boom Boom Slingshot, an active skill that fires a toy pellet for Break damage. Its passive partner is Break Techniques, which raises your Aniimo Break after twining, up to fifteen percent at the top level. Trailblazer three finishes the list with Twine Sync, a small final damage boost after twining that climbs to about five percent. These passives cost three cards each, so they are the expensive end of the tree, and you should plan your cards before you reach them. Remember that you earn cards slowly, from upgrade levels, Aniilog levels, quests and the Elite Challenge, so the sooner you start doing those, the sooner your build is complete. Nobody has to rush all three Trailblazer ranks in one week, and a steady routine works better than a sprint.

sections.heading: Talents that unlock evolutions
sections.script: Four talents have nothing to do with combat. They unlock exceptional evolutions. Dreamsong unlocks the exceptional evolution of Dreaple, Magic Horn does the same for Tromber, Peculiar Rock Ball for Bouldus, and Unwavering Rampart for Rookey. They sit at different ranks, from Student two up to Trailblazer one, and cost two or three cards. If you love one of those Aniimo, remember that the evolution is locked behind a Pathfinder talent, not only behind the Aniimo level. Many players hit the level and then wonder why nothing happens.

sections.heading: What to pick first
sections.script: Here is a sensible order. Take Master Trainer first. More experience from every catch and battle helps all your Aniimo, and guides keep recommending it early. Then Pro Catcher and Mode Switch if you catch a lot. Next, Boss Breaker, since Alpha bosses are where you spend your hardest fights. Quick Twine is worth the two cards because twining sits at the heart of combat. Keep the cards for the evolution talents until you really own the Aniimo they belong to. Finally, do not forget the active skills. Aeroboard saves stamina on long trips and Heal can save a fight, so use both from day one. Add the Bubble Gun later if you want to catch a rare Aniimo without risking a faint, because it lets you try again and again.

sections.heading: Common mistakes
sections.script: A few mistakes to avoid. Do not spend cards on a passive just because it is first in the list. Check what you actually need. Do not forget that the unlock is tied to your rank, so if a talent is missing, you probably have not passed that promotion yet. Do not ignore the Elite Pathfinder Challenge, because it is one of the ways to earn Report Cards. And remember that numbers on small bonuses can differ slightly between guides, because the game keeps changing. When in doubt, trust the in game Talents menu, which always shows the current values. One more tip: check which Aniimo you actually use before spending cards on an evolution talent. A talent for an Aniimo you never own is a wasted investment, while Master Trainer and Boss Breaker help every single team you will ever build, from your first week to the endgame.

sections.heading: Over to you
sections.script: Let us end with a joke. In Aniimo, the Bubble Gun keeps a wild Aniimo from fainting, which is more mercy than my own team ever gets. Now it is your turn. Which Pathfinder talent do you use the most, the Aeroboard, the Mega Mallet or the Bubble Gun, and which one did you only discover today? Tell us in the comments.
